name: Ghana
refrigerant_regulations: Permits required for bulk HFC imports
ewaste_legislation: Hazardous and Electronic Waste Control and Management Act (Act 917)
overview_en: Ghana faces significant e-waste challenges, particularly at the Agbogbloshie dumpsite in Accra, one of the world's largest informal e-waste recycling hubs. The cooling sector is growing rapidly, leading to increased imports of both new and used air conditioning units, many containing high-GWP refrigerants. The government has introduced legislation (Act 917) and MEPS (Minimum Energy Performance Standards) to regulate e-waste and appliance efficiency.
overview_fr: Le Ghana est confronté à d'importants défis en matière de déchets électroniques, en particulier à la décharge d'Agbogbloshie à Accra...

name: Nigeria
overview_en: Nigeria is a major destination for used electrical and electronic equipment (UEEE). Lagos ports receive significant volumes of illegal e-waste disguised as second-hand goods. The informal recycling sector is vast, leading to environmental contamination from crude extraction methods. The cooling sector is expanding, driving demand for refrigerants.
overview_fr: Le Nigeria est une destination majeure pour les équipements électriques et électroniques usagés...

name: Kenya
refrigerant_regulations: ODS and HFC tracking in place
ewaste_legislation: Environmental Management and Co-ordination (E-Waste Management) Regulations
overview_en: Kenya has emerging e-waste hubs and is making strides in formalizing recycling. The WEEE Centre in Nairobi is a notable formal recycling facility. The country has implemented MEPS for refrigeration and air conditioning. However, the influx of cheap, inefficient cooling appliances remains a challenge.
overview_fr: Le Kenya possède des pôles émergents de déchets électroniques et progresse dans la formalisation du recyclage...

name: South Africa
refrigerant_regulations: Strict controls on ODS, developing HFC phasedown
ewaste_legislation: National Environmental Management: Waste Act (EPR Regulations)
overview_en: South Africa has the most developed formal recycling infrastructure in Africa. It recently implemented mandatory Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for e-waste. The country has a substantial cooling market and is transitioning towards low-GWP refrigerants, with a strong manufacturing base for domestic appliances.
overview_fr: L'Afrique du Sud possède l'infrastructure de recyclage formelle la plus développée d'Afrique...

name: Egypt
overview_en: Egypt has a massive domestic market for cooling appliances due to its climate. E-waste recycling is primarily informal, though the government has launched initiatives like E-Tadweer to promote formal recycling. Recent waste management laws aim to organize the sector.
overview_fr: L'Égypte possède un marché intérieur massif pour les appareils de refroidissement en raison de son climat...

name: Côte d'Ivoire
overview_en: Côte d'Ivoire is developing its response to the growing e-waste problem. The informal sector handles the majority of e-waste dismantling. The country is working on finalizing a national legal framework for e-waste management and setting energy standards for appliances.
overview_fr: La Côte d'Ivoire développe sa réponse au problème croissant des déchets électroniques...

name: Senegal
overview_en: Senegal faces challenges with the importation of end-of-life cooling appliances, which often consume excessive energy and contain ozone-depleting substances. The government is actively working on projects to replace inefficient refrigerators and air conditioners.
overview_fr: Le Sénégal est confronté au défi de l'importation d'appareils de refroidissement en fin de vie...

name: Tanzania
overview_en: E-waste management in Tanzania is nascent, heavily reliant on informal collectors. The demand for cooling is rising, yet formal recycling infrastructure for refrigerants and electronic components remains limited. The government is drafting specific e-waste regulations.
overview_fr: La gestion des déchets électroniques en Tanzanie est naissante...

name: Ethiopia
overview_en: Ethiopia has established the Computer Refurbishment and Training Centre (CRTC) in Akaki, a significant step towards formal e-waste management. However, large quantities of unmanaged e-waste persist. The country is slowly integrating MEPS into its standards.
overview_fr: L'Éthiopie a créé le Centre de reconditionnement et de formation informatique (CRTC) à Akaki...

name: Morocco
refrigerant_regulations: Strict controls and certification for technicians
ewaste_legislation: Law 28-00 on Waste Management and Disposal
overview_en: Morocco is advancing in its waste management framework. While informal e-waste recycling exists, the government is exploring EPR systems. The cooling sector is well-regulated compared to regional peers, with technician training and certification programs for refrigerant handling.
overview_fr: Le Maroc progresse dans son cadre de gestion des déchets...
